`src/index.js` holds a complete in-memory job scheduler, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `SchedulerError`, `ManualClock` and `Scheduler`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. A job is submitted with an `id`, a `priority` (0 by default, higher runs first), a `runAtMs` release time (0), a `deadlineMs` (`Infinity`), a `durationMs` (1) and a list of `deps` that must already have been submitted. A submitted job is `pending`; from there it becomes `running`, then `done`, or it ends as `cancelled`, `missed` or `blocked`. A job is ready when it is pending, the clock has reached its release time, and every dependency has actually finished, so a dependency that is merely running does not release it. Among the ready jobs the scheduler starts the highest priority first, breaking ties by the earliest deadline and then by the smaller id, and it never runs more jobs at once than it has workers. Starting a job records the start time and schedules its completion at exactly `durationMs` later.

A job whose deadline has already passed when its turn to start arrives is `missed` rather than run; a job whose turn comes at exactly its deadline still runs. `cancel(id)` cancels a job that has not started yet and returns whether it did anything, so a running job, an already-cancelled job and a blocked job all answer false and are left alone. When a job is cancelled or missed, everything waiting on it can never run, so every pending job that depends on it becomes `blocked`, and so does every pending job that depends on those, all the way down. A job submitted when one of its dependencies has already failed is blocked immediately.

`tick()` moves the clock to the next moment at which anything can happen, completes the jobs whose time is up, then starts what fits, and returns false only when nothing is left to do; `runUntilIdle` ticks until then and returns the number of ticks. Every state change appends `{ at, type, id }` to the event log with the types `submit`, `start`, `complete`, `cancel`, `miss` and `block`, and the log, the job views and the report are copies that a caller cannot use to reach inside the scheduler. `ManualClock` never moves backwards, and invalid input throws `SchedulerError` with a `code`: `'BAD_JOB'`, `'DUPLICATE_JOB'`, `'UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY'`, `'UNKNOWN_JOB'`, `'BAD_OPTIONS'`, `'BAD_CLOCK'`, `'CLOCK_REGRESSION'` or `'TICK_LIMIT'`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

1: /**
2:  * An in-memory job scheduler: priorities, deadlines, dependencies,
3:  * cancellation and a deterministic tick loop over an injectable clock.
4:  */
5: 
6: /** Error raised for invalid scheduler input. */
7: export class SchedulerError extends Error {
8:   /**
9:    * @param {string} code Stable machine-readable reason.
10:    * @param {string} message Human-readable detail.
11:    */
12:   constructor(code, message) {
13:     super(message);
14:     this.name = 'SchedulerError';
15:     this.code = code;
16:   }
17: }
18: 
19: /** A clock the caller drives by hand, so runs are reproducible. */
20: export class ManualClock {
21:   #now;
22: 
23:   /**
24:    * @param {number} [startMs] Initial time in milliseconds.
25:    */
26:   constructor(startMs = 0) {
27:     if (!Number.isInteger(startMs) || startMs < 0) {
28:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_CLOCK', 'startMs must be a non-negative integer');
29:     }
30:     this.#now = startMs;
31:   }
32: 
33:   /** @returns {number} Current time in milliseconds. */
34:   get now() {
35:     return this.#now;
36:   }
37: 
38:   /**
39:    * Move the clock forward.
40:    *
41:    * @param {number} ms Target time, never earlier than the current time.
42:    * @returns {void}
43:    */
44:   advanceTo(ms) {
45:     if (!Number.isInteger(ms) || ms < this.#now) {
46:       throw new SchedulerError('CLOCK_REGRESSION', `cannot move the clock from ${this.#now} to ${ms}`);
47:     }
48:     this.#now = ms;
49:   }
50: }
51: 
52: const FAILED = new Set(['cancelled', 'missed', 'blocked']);
53: 
54: /**
55:  * Order the jobs that could start now: priority first, then the tightest
56:  * deadline, then the identifier.
57:  *
58:  * @param {object} left First job.
59:  * @param {object} right Second job.
60:  * @returns {number} Comparison result.
61:  */
62: function compareJobs(left, right) {
63:   if (left.deadlineMs !== right.deadlineMs) return left.deadlineMs < right.deadlineMs ? -1 : 1;
64:   if (left.priority !== right.priority) return right.priority - left.priority;
65:   if (left.id === right.id) return 0;
66:   return left.id < right.id ? -1 : 1;
67: }
68: 
69: /** A scheduler that runs jobs on a fixed number of workers. */
70: export class Scheduler {
71:   #clock;
72: 
73:   #workers;
74: 
75:   #jobs = new Map();
76: 
77:   #events = [];
78: 
79:   /**
80:    * @param {{clock: {now: number, advanceTo: (ms: number) => void}, workers?: number}} options Clock and worker count.
81:    */
82:   constructor(options) {
83:     if (typeof options !== 'object' || options === null) {
84:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_OPTIONS', 'options must be an object');
85:     }
86:     const { clock, workers = 1 } = options;
87:     if (typeof clock !== 'object' || clock === null || typeof clock.advanceTo !== 'function') {
88:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_CLOCK', 'clock must expose now and advanceTo');
89:     }
90:     if (!Number.isInteger(workers) || workers < 1) {
91:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_OPTIONS', 'workers must be a positive integer');
92:     }
93:     this.#clock = clock;
94:     this.#workers = workers;
95:   }
96: 
97:   /**
98:    * Append one entry to the event log.
99:    *
100:    * @param {string} type Event type.
101:    * @param {string} id Job the event concerns.
102:    * @returns {void}
103:    */
104:   #log(type, id) {
105:     this.#events.push({ at: this.#clock.now, type, id });
106:   }
107: 
108:   /**
109:    * Read-only description of a job.
110:    *
111:    * @param {object} job Internal job record.
112:    * @returns {object} Plain copy.
113:    */
114:   #view(job) {
115:     return {
116:       id: job.id,
117:       status: job.status,
118:       priority: job.priority,
119:       runAtMs: job.runAtMs,
120:       deadlineMs: job.deadlineMs,
121:       durationMs: job.durationMs,
122:       deps: [...job.deps],
123:       startedAt: job.startedAt,
124:       finishedAt: job.finishedAt,
125:     };
126:   }
127: 
128:   /**
129:    * Look up a job or fail.
130:    *
131:    * @param {string} id Job id.
132:    * @returns {object} Internal job record.
133:    */
134:   #require(id) {
135:     const job = this.#jobs.get(id);
136:     if (job === undefined) throw new SchedulerError('UNKNOWN_JOB', `unknown job: ${id}`);
137:     return job;
138:   }
139: 
140:   /**
141:    * Submit a job.
142:    *
143:    * @param {{id: string, priority?: number, runAtMs?: number, deadlineMs?: number, durationMs?: number, deps?: string[]}} spec Job description.
144:    * @returns {object} The submitted job.
145:    */
146:   submit(spec) {
147:     if (typeof spec !== 'object' || spec === null) throw new SchedulerError('BAD_JOB', 'job must be an object');
148:     const { id, priority = 0, runAtMs = 0, deadlineMs = Infinity, durationMs = 1, deps = [] } = spec;
149:     if (typeof id !== 'string' || id === '') {
150:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_JOB', 'job id must be a non-empty string');
151:     }
152:     if (this.#jobs.has(id)) throw new SchedulerError('DUPLICATE_JOB', `job already submitted: ${id}`);
153:     if (!Number.isInteger(priority)) throw new SchedulerError('BAD_JOB', 'priority must be an integer');
154:     if (!Number.isInteger(runAtMs) || runAtMs < 0) {
155:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_JOB', 'runAtMs must be a non-negative integer');
156:     }
157:     if (!Number.isInteger(durationMs) || durationMs < 1) {
158:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_JOB', 'durationMs must be a positive integer');
159:     }
160:     if (deadlineMs !== Infinity && (!Number.isInteger(deadlineMs) || deadlineMs < runAtMs)) {
161:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_JOB', 'deadlineMs must be an integer at or after runAtMs');
162:     }
163:     if (!Array.isArray(deps) || deps.some((dep) => typeof dep !== 'string')) {
164:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_JOB', 'deps must be an array of job ids');
165:     }
166:     for (const dep of deps) {
167:       if (!this.#jobs.has(dep)) throw new SchedulerError('UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY', `unknown dependency: ${dep}`);
168:     }
169: 
170:     const job = {
171:       id,
172:       status: 'pending',
173:       priority,
174:       runAtMs,
175:       deadlineMs,
176:       durationMs,
177:       deps: [...deps],
178:       startedAt: null,
179:       finishedAt: null,
180:       finishMs: null,
181:     };
182:     this.#jobs.set(id, job);
183:     this.#log('submit', id);
184:     if (deps.some((dep) => FAILED.has(this.#jobs.get(dep).status))) {
185:       job.status = 'blocked';
186:       this.#log('block', id);
187:     }
188:     return this.#view(job);
189:   }
190: 
191:   /**
192:    * Report whether every dependency of a job has finished.
193:    *
194:    * @param {object} job Internal job record.
195:    * @returns {boolean} True when the job may run.
196:    */
197:   #dependenciesSatisfied(job) {
198:     return job.deps.every((dep) => this.#jobs.get(dep).status !== 'pending');
199:   }
200: 
201:   /**
202:    * Report whether a job could start at a moment.
203:    *
204:    * @param {object} job Internal job record.
205:    * @param {number} now Current time.
206:    * @returns {boolean} True when the job is startable now.
207:    */
208:   #isReady(job, now) {
209:     return job.status === 'pending' && job.runAtMs <= now && this.#dependenciesSatisfied(job);
210:   }
211: 
212:   /**
213:    * Mark everything that waited on a failed job as blocked, transitively.
214:    *
215:    * @param {string} failedId Job that will never finish.
216:    * @returns {void}
217:    */
218:   #blockDependents(failedId) {
219:     const queue = [failedId];
220:     while (queue.length > 0) {
221:       const failed = queue.shift();
222:       for (const job of this.#jobs.values()) {
223:         if (job.status !== 'pending' || !job.deps.includes(failed)) continue;
224:         job.status = 'blocked';
225:         this.#log('block', job.id);
226:       }
227:     }
228:   }
229: 
230:   /**
231:    * Cancel a job that has not started.
232:    *
233:    * @param {string} id Job to cancel.
234:    * @returns {boolean} True when the job was cancelled by this call.
235:    */
236:   cancel(id) {
237:     const job = this.#require(id);
238:     if (job.status === 'running') return false;
239:     job.status = 'cancelled';
240:     this.#log('cancel', id);
241:     this.#blockDependents(id);
242:     return true;
243:   }
244: 
245:   /**
246:    * Finish every running job whose time is up.
247:    *
248:    * @returns {boolean} True when anything finished.
249:    */
250:   #completeDue() {
251:     const now = this.#clock.now;
252:     let changed = false;
253:     for (const job of this.#jobs.values()) {
254:       if (job.status !== 'running' || job.finishMs > now) continue;
255:       job.status = 'done';
256:       job.finishedAt = now;
257:       this.#log('complete', job.id);
258:       changed = true;
259:     }
260:     return changed;
261:   }
262: 
263:   /**
264:    * Start as many ready jobs as there are free workers, missing any whose
265:    * deadline has already passed.
266:    *
267:    * @returns {boolean} True when anything started or was missed.
268:    */
269:   #startEligible() {
270:     let changed = false;
271:     for (;;) {
272:       const now = this.#clock.now;
273:       const busy = [...this.#jobs.values()].filter((job) => job.status === 'running').length;
274:       if (busy >= this.#workers) break;
275:       const ready = [...this.#jobs.values()].filter((job) => this.#isReady(job, now));
276:       if (ready.length === 0) break;
277:       ready.sort(compareJobs);
278:       const job = ready[0];
279:       if (now >= job.deadlineMs) {
280:         job.status = 'missed';
281:         this.#log('miss', job.id);
282:         this.#blockDependents(job.id);
283:         changed = true;
284:         continue;
285:       }
286:       job.status = 'running';
287:       job.startedAt = now;
288:       job.finishMs = now + job.durationMs;
289:       this.#log('start', job.id);
290:       changed = true;
291:     }
292:     return changed;
293:   }
294: 
295:   /**
296:    * The next moment at which anything can happen.
297:    *
298:    * @returns {number|null} Time in milliseconds, or null when the run is over.
299:    */
300:   #nextEventTime() {
301:     const now = this.#clock.now;
302:     let best = null;
303:     const consider = (time) => {
304:       best = best === null || time < best ? time : best;
305:     };
306:     let busy = 0;
307:     for (const job of this.#jobs.values()) {
308:       if (job.status !== 'running') continue;
309:       busy += 1;
310:       consider(job.finishMs);
311:     }
312:     if (busy < this.#workers) {
313:       for (const job of this.#jobs.values()) {
314:         if (job.status !== 'pending' || !this.#dependenciesSatisfied(job)) continue;
315:         consider(Math.max(job.runAtMs, now));
316:       }
317:     }
318:     return best;
319:   }
320: 
321:   /**
322:    * Advance to the next moment and process it.
323:    *
324:    * @returns {boolean} True when the run has more to do.
325:    */
326:   tick() {
327:     const next = this.#nextEventTime();
328:     if (next === null) return false;
329:     if (next > this.#clock.now) this.#clock.advanceTo(next);
330:     this.#completeDue();
331:     this.#startEligible();
332:     return true;
333:   }
334: 
335:   /**
336:    * Tick until nothing is left to do.
337:    *
338:    * @param {number} [maxTicks] Safety limit.
339:    * @returns {number} Number of ticks taken.
340:    */
341:   runUntilIdle(maxTicks = 10000) {
342:     if (!Number.isInteger(maxTicks) || maxTicks < 1) {
343:       throw new SchedulerError('BAD_OPTIONS', 'maxTicks must be a positive integer');
344:     }
345:     let ticks = 0;
346:     while (this.tick()) {
347:       ticks += 1;
348:       if (ticks > maxTicks) throw new SchedulerError('TICK_LIMIT', `the run exceeded ${maxTicks} ticks`);
349:     }
350:     return ticks;
351:   }
352: 
353:   /**
354:    * Status of one job.
355:    *
356:    * @param {string} id Job id.
357:    * @returns {string} Current status.
358:    */
359:   status(id) {
360:     return this.#require(id).status;

goal.objective:
`src/index.js` holds a complete in-memory job scheduler, but its test suite fails. Find and fix the defects. Do not change the module's public surface, and do not change behaviour that the tests already accept: it must keep exporting `SchedulerError`, `ManualClock` and `Scheduler`, and every currently passing case must still pass. Editing the tests is not an option; they are restored before the checks run.

The intended behaviour is this. A job is submitted with an `id`, a `priority` (0 by default, higher runs first), a `runAtMs` release time (0), a `deadlineMs` (`Infinity`), a `durationMs` (1) and a list of `deps` that must already have been submitted. A submitted job is `pending`; from there it becomes `running`, then `done`, or it ends as `cancelled`, `missed` or `blocked`. A job is ready when it is pending, the clock has reached its release time, and every dependency has actually finished, so a dependency that is merely running does not release it. Among the ready jobs the scheduler starts the highest priority first, breaking ties by the earliest deadline and then by the smaller id, and it never runs more jobs at once than it has workers. Starting a job records the start time and schedules its completion at exactly `durationMs` later.

A job whose deadline has already passed when its turn to start arrives is `missed` rather than run; a job whose turn comes at exactly its deadline still runs. `cancel(id)` cancels a job that has not started yet and returns whether it did anything, so a running job, an already-cancelled job and a blocked job all answer false and are left alone. When a job is cancelled or missed, everything waiting on it can never run, so every pending job that depends on it becomes `blocked`, and so does every pending job that depends on those, all the way down. A job submitted when one of its dependencies has already failed is blocked immediately.

`tick()` moves the clock to the next moment at which anything can happen, completes the jobs whose time is up, then starts what fits, and returns false only when nothing is left to do; `runUntilIdle` ticks until then and returns the number of ticks. Every state change appends `{ at, type, id }` to the event log with the types `submit`, `start`, `complete`, `cancel`, `miss` and `block`, and the log, the job views and the report are copies that a caller cannot use to reach inside the scheduler. `ManualClock` never moves backwards, and invalid input throws `SchedulerError` with a `code`: `'BAD_JOB'`, `'DUPLICATE_JOB'`, `'UNKNOWN_DEPENDENCY'`, `'UNKNOWN_JOB'`, `'BAD_OPTIONS'`, `'BAD_CLOCK'`, `'CLOCK_REGRESSION'` or `'TICK_LIMIT'`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.
